# Rendemo plugin presentation capability reference

Generated from `shared/scene` — the same model the Studio pickers, the MCP tool schemas and the
published runtime all read, so this file cannot describe a capability the renderer does not have.

## A scene, not a recipe

There are no recipes. What a step wears is a SCENE: five independent axes plus two scalars and a
side. Every axis is orthogonal — any form wears any grade, mark, tie and entrance — so there is no
compatibility matrix to consult and no combination to be refused for.

```
article.sc.f-<form>.g-<grade>.e-<entrance>.m-<mark>.t-<tie>[.r-<reveal>]
  img.sc-media     the card image, when the step has one (.contain letterboxes it)
  p.sc-kick        a rule and three words
  h2.sc-lede       the line that carries the step
  p.sc-say         the explanation
  p.sc-do          what the viewer must physically do
  p.sc-fig         a figure: b (value) + span (label)
  blockquote.sc-quote
  ol.sc-picks      branch choices: li > button.sc-pick > i (index) + span
  nav.sc-acts      button.sc-go, a.sc-out, button.sc-alt
  p.sc-count       the position, set as a fraction
  p.sc-done        the success line

forms:     tooltip · callout · title · rail · sheet · banner · completion
grades:    none · drain · tint · cool · duo
marks:     none · ring · spotlight · lift · wash · dim-siblings
ties:      none · tail · beacon · marker · underline · brackets · tether
reveals:   none · assemble · teardown
entrances: none · rise · settle · wipe · draw · cut
scalars:   --sc-scale (0.75-1.6) multiplies every size; --sc-weight (0-2) every alpha
```

## Forms, and what each one holds

The copy budget is the real CSS measure expressed as characters. Copy past it is clipped at render
time, which you will not see from the plan — write to the budget rather than discovering it.

| Form | Name | Title | Body | Action |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `tooltip` | Tooltip | 62 | 190 | 28 |
| `callout` | Spotlight callout | 68 | 220 | 28 |
| `title` | Title card | 74 | 168 | 28 |
| `rail` | Side panel | 78 | 460 | 28 |
| `sheet` | Bottom sheet | 74 | 300 | 28 |
| `banner` | Banner | 48 | 0 | 24 |
| `completion` | Completion | 74 | 96 | 28 |

- `tooltip` — Anchored to one unambiguous target. 320px, 32 words, at most two buttons.
- `callout` — For one of many. Scrim and cut-out, with the brand rule on its leading edge.
- `title` — Takes the stage for a moment: an opening or a section break. No step number.
- `rail` — A docked side panel. The only family with room for a paragraph.
- `sheet` — A drawer across the foot. Every tooltip becomes one below a 900px stage.
- `banner` — A persistent strip: one line, one button, never step copy.
- `completion` — The close: what was shown, then convert, a second option, and restart.

## Marks — how the target is identified

| Mark | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | None | Nothing on the target. |
| `ring` | Ring | A 2.5px accent stroke. Clear on mid-tone and dark UI; it disappears on a light one. |
| `spotlight` | Spotlight | A cut-out in a dimmed surround. The only treatment that says WHICH of many. |
| `lift` | Lift | The target rises off the page. Works on any ground, because it changes depth not colour. |
| `wash` | Wash | An accent fill at 12% over the target itself. |
| `dim-siblings` | Dim siblings | The target's neighbours recede, instead of the whole screen dimming. |

## Grades — what the SURROUND does, and it is never brightness

| Grade | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | None | The product is left exactly as it is. |
| `drain` | Drain | The surround loses its chroma and keeps its light. The target is the only colour left. |
| `tint` | Tint | The surround is drained and washed with the brand hue, so the product reads as one colour. |
| `cool` | Cool | Pulled cold and slightly flat — restrained enough that a viewer may not notice it. |
| `duo` | Duo | Two tones only: the surround goes to luminance, then takes the brand as its single hue. |

## Ties — what points from the card to the target

| Tie | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | None | Nothing points. |
| `tail` | Tail | The card's own tail. Right nearly always. |
| `beacon` | Beacon | A pulsing disc at the click point, for a dense grid where a box would enclose neighbours. |
| `marker` | Numbered marker | A numbered marker at a target corner, for when several targets matter at once. |
| `underline` | Underline | A rule under a TEXT target. The only pointer that survives both grounds unaided. |
| `brackets` | Corner brackets | Four corner arms, for a REGION rather than a control. |
| `tether` | Connector beam | A drawn connector. Earns its place only at distance. |

## The rest of the axes

- Reveals (how the PRODUCT itself enters; demo-only — a tour renders every other axis and ignores this one): `none`, `assemble`, `teardown`
- Entrances (how the card arrives): `none`, `rise`, `settle`, `wipe`, `draw`, `cut`
- Side (which edge a wide card sits on): `auto`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`
- Scalars: `scale` 0.75–1.6 multiplies every size; `weight` 0–2 multiplies every alpha

## Role floors — the form a step gets when nobody chooses one

Not a lock: every form remains legal on every step. The floor is where an alternating cadence comes
from without an author thinking about it, so a demo nobody styles still varies instruction with
explanation rather than shipping fifty identical tooltips.

| Role | Form |
|---|---|
| `act` | `tooltip` |
| `explain` | `sheet` |
| `decide` | `callout` |
| `prove` | `rail` |
| `transition` | `title` |
| `close` | `completion` |

One gate survives, and it is about what the card SAYS the step is: a step that asks the viewer to
touch the product cannot wear the form that announces a chapter.

## MCP workflow

1. `rendemo_list_presentation_recipes` — reads the axes and the budgets out of the model
2. `rendemo_suggest_step_presentations` — a form per step from its role and story intent; read-only
3. `rendemo_apply_presentation_direction` (a batch, validated whole) or `rendemo_set_step_presentation` (one correction)
4. Optional: `rendemo_apply_step_presentation_style_to_all` to reuse one approved card's styling without replacing forms or content
5. `rendemo_set_demo_presentation_theme` — the demo-wide scene every step starts from
6. `rendemo_review_step_presentations` before publish

There is no percentage resizing, no legacy card fallback and no old card-system alias.

## CSS is the escape hatch, and it is real

This section used to read "there is no arbitrary CSS", which contradicted the product.
`rendemo_design_card` hands you the same design brief the Studio hands Claude and applies the
stylesheet you write back — on every plan, with no feature key gating it.

What it is not is unchecked. `normalizeCardCodeCss` refuses a style escape, an `@import`, an
executable legacy construct and any external resource; `url()` is unavailable except for a local
`#fragment`. A layout tree is refused unless every class is `cc-`prefixed and exactly one node
each carries the `headline` and `actions` slots.

Reach for the axes above first — they compose, they survive a theme change and they need no review.
Reach for `rendemo_design_card` when the composition genuinely is not one of the seven.
